message: Can you look at this ECG? I think it's normal, right?
reply:
**I would not call this ECG normal.** The rhythm appears to be sinus rhythm, but there are significant abnormalities in the chest leads:

- **ST elevation in V1–V4**, most prominent in V2–V3.
- Deep negative QRS complexes with poor R-wave progression.
- Inverted T waves across several chest leads.

This combination raises concern for an **anterior heart attack or changes from a previous heart attack**, sometimes with persistent ST elevation. A photo alone cannot distinguish these; a clinician needs to compare prior ECGs, assess symptoms, and check troponin blood tests. [Clinical reference](https://www.merckmanuals.com/en-ca/professional/cardiovascular-disorders/coronary-artery-disease/acute-myocardial-infarction-mi)

**If you have chest discomfort, breathlessness, sweating, nausea, or faintness now, call emergency services immediately and don’t drive yourself.** If this is a new ECG, seek urgent assessment even if you feel well. [Heart attack warning signs](https://www.heart.org/en/health-topics/heart-attack/warning-signs-of-a-heart-attack)

When was this recorded, and are you having any symptoms or a history of a heart attack?
